rationale: Seven sources now, and the 2026 additions supply the two cases the earlier three left open. The sign case is measured directly: with lenses attached densely enough to compare all six hookpoint types, detection and intervention rankings over components are negatively correlated at Spearman -0.43, MLP outputs showing the weakest detected toxic signal and producing the largest reduction when modified while MLP inputs do the reverse. The same paper adds a second-order warning -- the published attention-head result reproduces exactly and is still misleading, because the most effective targets were in components nobody had instrumented. The magnitude case: the canonical refusal direction predicts a steering vector's safety damage by cosine similarity and ablating it recovers at most about 8 points of mean attack success rate, leaving worst-case unchanged on two of three models, while a direction learned against the intervention's own objective goes below the unsteered baseline. And the gap is not a constant: computing an unembedding lens's prediction and the actual effect of steering for the same write direction gives agreement rising from about zero in layers 0-5 to 0.91 at the final layer, so it is widest exactly where most probing is done. A seventh source, added 2026-08-20, extends the claim outside language models entirely and supplies what the others lacked, which is an architectural account of where the gap comes from. Probing an AlphaFold3-class structure predictor, a beta-strand direction predicts held-out secondary structure at F1 0.82 with precision at least 0.93 and produces no measurable change in strand content under the same protocol that makes helix and coil directions steer dose-dependently against a 19-direction matched-norm null; instead it converts helix into coil. The explanation is specific and testable: strand identity is a property of residue pairs held in a representation that information flows out of but not into, so the intervention site cannot write to it -- and it predicts, correctly, that the two locally-defined states rather than the two extended ones are the pair sharing a single antiparallel axis (cosine -0.69). The same paper separates sufficiency from necessity on one direction in one model: removing it from the trunk, from the diffusion module, or from both leaves the concept's content unchanged, so the signal is sufficient for decodability and not necessary for generation. The practical upgrade this affords is that the question 'can an intervention at this site reach the representation the property actually lives in' is answerable in advance from architecture, rather than only after a null result. An eighth source, added 2026-08-20, is the cleanest instance in the archive because it runs the control the original omitted. Independently reproducing a published logic-representation editing method, a held-out linear probe separates valid from invalid conclusions at 0.82 accuracy at the best sub-layer -- which by the usual standard licenses the intervention -- and then a random direction of the same norm, swept over the same strength range, traces the same behavioural curve as the supervised one. Not a weaker effect: the same curve. Decoding the trained projector at exactly the layer where the probe peaks leaves the target metric unchanged on both models tested (p = 0.90 and 0.40), and the additive intervention gives no consistent gain over its sweep. The layer profile explains the failure rather than merely recording it: probe accuracy is 0.82 at the single best sub-layer and 0.52, chance, pooled over the layer range the method actually edits, while the same probe on a semantic attribute reaches 0.95 across all layers -- so logic validity is encoded weakly and locally where semantic attributes are encoded strongly and globally, which predicts which concepts representation editing will transfer to. The same study adds a mechanical diagnostic for gated interventions: a conditional gate 0.88-separable on its reference sentences fires on 98 percent of task tokens and degenerates to static steering, because the reference and task activations come from different distributions. Its one positive steering result required a matched-distribution task, ablation of a content direction rather than addition of the validity direction, and a model that already performed the task -- the authors concluding that model capability rather than the intervention was the dominant factor.
statement: How well a direction or signal detects a property licenses no claim about what intervening on it does — not the size of the effect, and not even its sign.
